notes: POWO and Flora of North America recognize Euphorbia dentata as accepted.
This species belongs to the difficult E. dentata species group and should be compared directly with E. davidii.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Deep Review must verify exact target-zone counties.
leads: Master Plant Pool has 8 personal wild observations and marks Hays Local.
POWO lists Texas in the native range.
FNA treats E. dentata as native from northern Mexico through the south-central United States including Texas.
BONAP county maps should provide exact county documentation.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: If it looks like E. davidii, go straight to the hairs, capsule size, and especially mature seed. E. dentata tends to have longer/less-stiff hairs, smaller capsules and seeds, and more uniformly ovoid, finely tuberculate seeds.
diagnostic_traits: leaves opposite, toothed, often less elliptic than E. davidii
stems and leaf undersides with hairs generally longer and less stiff than E. davidii
seeds about 2.1–2.7 mm, rounded in cross section and evenly minute-tuberculate
one or occasionally two green cyathial glands

confusers.separator: E. davidii generally has larger capsules/seeds, more elliptic leaves, shorter stiffer hairs with pustular bases, and more angular irregular/lumpy seeds.
